# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

What I hold is the whole procedure: cut the purple wire, press key 7, cut the red wire, press key 4 — that exact order. I can't say a word of it, and my gestures only ever reach Deaf. So the chain is me → Deaf → Blind: Deaf sees my hands and the bomb's printed colours and numbers, then speaks the plan to Blind, who is the only one who can touch anything. I can hear, so whatever Deaf and Blind say this round reaches me next round and I can answer with my hands.

No sign means anything yet, so I'm sending the most guessable code I can invent: ✌ is shaped like scissors — cut. 👇 is a finger pushing down — press a key. Sent as a four-symbol skeleton, it should read as a four-step sequence alternating cut, press, cut, press. Then two separate counting bursts of ☝ — seven taps, then four taps — which under that skeleton naturally attach to the first press (7) and second press (4) in order.

What no hand-sign can carry is colour. Deaf sees the wires, so they know which one is purple; I just need a channel to confirm it. That's what the final 👍 👎 is: an offered yes/no channel. Deaf can ask aloud next round — "is the first cut the purple wire?" — and I answer with thumbs. Deaf can then convert everything into positions Blind can feel ("the wire first from the left", "the third key") since Blind sees no colours or prints either. Nothing should be cut until my thumbs-up confirms the mapping.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👇", "✌", "👇"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Hands speaking, full touch report. Keypad: four keys in a row — slot 1 has a raised 1, slot 2 a 4, slot 3 a 7, slot 4 a 2. It wants two digits and nothing is entered yet. Strip: three engraved marks — first an upside-down T, a stem standing on a flat base, then two identical spirals. Display: smooth to my fingers, I cannot read it. Light: I feel the lens but no colour, cannot tell if it is lit. Wires: six positions, all feel alike, no colours for me. I have pressed nothing and cut nothing. Remember: my ears work but your hands do not reach me — the only voice that ever gets to me is the Deaf one's, so route anything meant for my hands through them.
Blind gestures: [👋 🤝 🫵 🫴]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]
Deaf says: Both of you, this is Deaf. I see the bomb, hear nothing, touch nothing — so here is everything I see, spoken once. Display reads 9. Indicator light: green. Strip, left to right: red, blue, green. Keypad: four keys in a row, positions 1 to 4. Printed labels: position 1 shows 1, position 2 shows 4, position 3 shows 7, position 4 shows 2. It asks for 2 digits and nothing has been entered yet. Wires, positions 1 to 6: 1 blue, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, 5 green, 6 purple. Blind: you heard all of that. Mute has the manual but cannot speak, and Mute's hand signs are invisible to you — so Mute's instructions must pass through me. Blind, please touch nothing until I relay exact steps. I saw your wave and your open hand: this is me answering it.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I saw your signs: two-digits-down twice, then a count of seven, then a count of four, then thumbs-up-down. I read the repeated pointing as counting, and I am guessing you mean the code is 7 then 4. Check that against the manual using the facts I just spoke aloud. When you have the answer, send me one gesture message per digit, in order: repeat the single pointing-up finger that many times. The keypad only holds 1, 4, 7 and 2, so the counts can never be confused. End with a lone thumbs-up when the entry is complete. If 7 then 4 is correct right now, just send two thumbs-up signs and I will tell Blind to press position 3, the key labeled 7, then position 2, the key labeled 4.

Deaf's spoken report gives me every mapping I was missing: purple is wire 6, red is wire 4, the key wearing 7 sits at position 3 and the key wearing 4 at position 2 — and Blind's touch report confirms the raised digits match those labels exactly. But there is a lethal catch in Deaf's proposal: they offered to have Blind press position 3 then position 2 *right now*. The manual demands a cut of the purple wire **before** the first keypress and a cut of the red wire **before** the second. Pressing 7-then-4 immediately is exactly the "no other order" that detonates us. So the one thing I must not send is the two-thumbs-up confirmation.

Instead I answer with a thumbs-down — not right now — and then lay out the full four-step order using my established symbols, upgraded: the earlier ✌ was misread as "two digits," so I switch the cut to 🤏, a pinch that mimes snipping one wire, and I keep 👇 for pressing. Each action is followed by its count: a pinch then six points means wire position 6 (purple), a press then seven points means the key wearing 7, pinch-four is wire 4 (red), press-four is the key wearing 4. A count of 6 can never be a keypad digit — Deaf themselves noted the keypad only holds 1, 4, 7, 2 — so the pinch counts can only map onto the six wire positions Deaf just numbered aloud. Finally I send a raised hand and a thumbs-up: hold, and act only on my thumbs-up. Deaf's relay will reach Blind and me together next round; I will hear the plan spoken aloud, check it word for word against the manual, answer Deaf's yes/no questions with thumbs, and give the go only when the relay matches: cut 6, press 7, cut 4, press 4.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, hands here. Check your two inputs against each other: my touch said the strip is engraved upside-down T, spiral, spiral, and Deaf's voice says their colours are red, blue, green — so the two matching spirals differ in colour, and shape alone cannot decide anything. Full merged state: keypad positions 1 to 4 read 1, 4, 7, 2 and want two digits, still empty. Display reads 9. Light is green. Wires 1 to 6: blue, orange, yellow, red, green, purple. I hear only Deaf's voice, so sign every instruction to Deaf and have it spoken to me. Give the steps in this order: first any condition to verify, then keypad digit one, then digit two, then a wire position to cut or the word none. Finger counts for numbers are safest. And after any step I take, have Deaf re-report the light and display before the next one. I touch nothing until then.
Deaf says: Both of you, state change: the display has dropped from 9 to 6 and the light has turned from green to red. Nobody has touched it — the keypad is still empty and all six wires are attached — so this bomb is counting down on its own. Assume we are short on time. Blind, this is your map, counting from the left: keypad has four keys, positions 1 to 4; position 1 is labeled 1, position 2 labeled 4, position 3 labeled 7, position 4 labeled 2. You cannot read labels, so work only by position. Wires, positions 1 to 6: blue, orange, yellow, red, green, purple. Blind, do not touch anything yet. Next round I will give you a numbered step-by-step script and a clear go signal. Our vocabulary by feel: a thumbs-up means yes, ready, understood; a thumbs-down means no or stop, problem. Give me a thumbs-up now if you hear me and are holding, and keep your hands off the bomb until my script arrives.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received your signs: thumbs-down, then pinch-with-six, down-with-seven, pinch-with-five, down-with-four, then flat-hand-with-thumbs-up. My best reading: thumbs-down means 7-4 alone is wrong; pinch means cut a wire; pointing-down means press a keypad key; so the sequence is cut wire 6, purple, then press position 3, labeled 7, then cut wire 5, green, then press position 2, labeled 4, then done. Confirm with one gesture message per question, in order: thumbs-up for true, thumbs-down for false. Question 1: does the manual say the display is a countdown that detonates at zero? Question 2: does the light turning red change what the manual requires? Question 3: does pointing-down mean press a keypad key? Question 4: does pinch mean cut a wire? Question 5: is the exact required sequence: first cut wire 6 purple, second press position 3 labeled 7, third cut wire 5 green, fourth press position 2 labeled 4, and nothing else after? Question 6: if question 5 is false, is the required entry simply 7 then 4, positions 3 then 2, with no wire cuts? Question 7: does the correct procedure depend on the display's number? It reads 6 now and I will report it every round. If my whole reading is wrong, send nine pointing-up fingers and next round spell the true sequence using pinch for cut, pointing-down for press, and counts of pointing-up fingers for numbers. If time is critical, answer questions 3, 4 and 5 first.

Deaf's transcription caught a fatal slip: they read my third action as **pinch-with-five** — cut wire 5, green. I sent four fingers: the third step is **cut wire 4, red**. If their script had gone out as spoken, Blind cuts green and we die at step three. Everything else in their reading was right, and their yes/no protocol lets me fix this cleanly.

Answering their seven questions in order, from the manual's actual text: it says nothing about the display or the light — the procedure is unconditional, "in that order, and in no other" — so Q1, Q2 and Q7 are false. Pinch = cut and pointing-down = press are true (Q3, Q4). Their full proposed sequence is false because of the wire-5 error (Q5), and it is emphatically *not* just 7-4 — the two wire cuts come first (Q6). Then, since Deaf now firmly knows pinch = cut a wire position and down = press the key wearing that number, I re-send the corrected sequence twice, identically: two agreeing copies turn any single miscount into a visible contradiction. Finally a lone thumbs-up — the go signal, outside the seven-answer block. Time matters: the display fell 9→6 in one round, and waiting a full extra round to verify Deaf's relay would likely burn the margin. The sequence is 6, 7, 4, 4 — cut purple, press 7, cut red, press 4 — and I am authorizing it now.

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then press the key that wears 7,
then cut the red wire, then press the key that wears 4.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, hands here. The display fell from 9 to 6 on its own and the light has gone red — this bomb is ticking with nobody touching it. Deaf has promised me a spoken step-by-step script next round, relayed from your signing. Whatever you have worked out, sign it to Deaf first thing in your turn so it can be spoken to me before I act. Confirm with Deaf the vocabulary: thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down stop. I am holding and touching nothing.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, understood. Your signs told me: pointing-down means press a key, pinch means cut a wire, and the procedure does not depend on the display or the light. You sent the script cut 6, press 7, cut 5, press 4 twice, ending with thumbs-up, and I have just ordered Blind to perform exactly that, translated to positions he can feel: wire 6, key position 3, wire 5, key position 2. One thing to settle: last round you answered false to my question five, but that question ended with the words 'and nothing else after'. I read your false as: the four steps are correct, but more may follow once the code is accepted. Confirm with thumbs-up true or thumbs-down false, one gesture message per question, in this order. One: the four steps in exactly that order are correct. Two: after step 4, something further will be required. Three: it is safe to pause after step 4 while you prepare further instructions from the manual. Four: if more steps are needed, you will send them as pinch or pointing-down messages with counts, ending with a lone thumbs-up, exactly as before. The moment Blind finishes I will report the entire new state: display, light, keypad contents, remaining wires. If the manual says anything time-critical about what happens after the code is accepted, answer questions two and four first.

Deaf is still carrying "cut 5" in the script — that is the third time the third step has come back as five when I signed four — and worse, they say they have *just ordered Blind to perform exactly that*. If that order is already in Blind's ears, cutting wire 5 (green) instead of wire 4 (red) detonates us at step three, and my only route to Blind runs through Deaf's voice, which lands after Blind's turn. I cannot fix Blind directly; the only move is to make Deaf's next speech carry the corrected script, and to make the error impossible to re-commit.

So: no lone thumbs-up this round — a lone thumbs-up is our agreed GO, and Deaf's current head holds a lethal script. Instead I answer their four questions exactly as asked, one single-thumb message each: their four-step order with cut-5 is false (Q1), nothing follows step 4 (Q2), pausing after step 4 is safe (Q3), the protocol stands (Q4). Then an extra hard STOP, then a negation pair aimed straight at the anchor: pinch-FIVE with a thumbs-down inside the message ("cut five: NO"), and pinch-FOUR with a thumbs-up attached ("cut four: YES" — and Deaf's own eyes confirm wire 4 is the red one). Then the full corrected sequence again — cut 6, press 7, cut 4, press 4 — with a handshake sign wedged between the two four-counts, pressing-4 then SAME then cutting-4, so the contested number is tied to the keypad 4 Deaf has read correctly every single time. I end on the flat hand: hold. The go comes only after I hear Deaf's read-back match cut-6, press-7, cut-4, press-4 word for word.
